title: Natural numbers as sets: infinity, induction, and arithmetic
summary: The least inductive set realizes the natural numbers and their unique arithmetic structure.
abstract: The natural numbers can be realized as sets, with each number containing all the smaller numbers. The axiom of infinity ensures that all these finite stages belong to one set. Within it, zero and the next-number operation satisfy induction: any selection containing zero and closed under taking the next number contains every natural number. These properties determine the natural-number system up to a unique matching, including its familiar order, addition, and multiplication.
